result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.volume()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the volume of a set of nodes (the sum of their degrees). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L55309-L55358){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.volume( S, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Volume](/assets/graphs/volume.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph and set S = A, B, C, with each member's degree in a badge: A 2, B 3, C 4. The volume of S is the sum of its degrees, 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.0, which counts the edge ends S holds, including its three edges to the rest." width="100%"} The volume of a node set is the sum of its members' degrees (out-degrees on a directed graph, total edge weight on a weighted one): roughly, how many edge ends the set holds. It is the size measure used to normalize cuts, so that `conductance()` and `normalized_cut_size()` compare a cut against how much the set is connected overall, rather than how many nodes it has. `S=` is treated as a set: a node listed twice is counted once (NetworkX would count its degree twice). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to sum weighted degrees. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The volume. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty or a node does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The three nodes of one triangle in the two-triangle graph have degrees 2, 2 and 3: ::: {#b3e8f744 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) graph.volume(["A", "B", "C"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 7.0 ``` ::: :::
